course.title: Web Dev for Beginners
course.subtitle: HTML, CSS and JavaScript learned by building real things — terrariums, games and banks.

course.after_note: Build your own project — a portfolio page is the classic next move. The tree's JavaScript, GenAI and Copilot tracks continue from here.

modules.title: Getting started
modules.blurb: The tools of the trade, working like a team, and building for everyone.

lessons.title: Intro to programming languages and tools of the trade
lessons.objective: What programming languages are, and the software professionals use.
keys: A language is a contract between you and the machine — the tools just enforce it
The professional kit: editor (VS Code), browser dev tools, terminal, git
Learn concepts, not syntax — syntax is searchable, concepts compound

lessons.title: Intro to GitHub — working with a team
lessons.objective: Collaborate on a code base with branches and pull requests.
keys: clone → branch → commit → PR → review → merge: the team loop
A commit message is a note to your future teammates — and future you
The PR is where code review lives; small PRs get good reviews

lessons.title: Accessibility fundamentals
lessons.objective: The basics of building web pages everyone can use.
keys: Accessibility is engineering, not charity — 1 in 5 users depends on it
Semantic HTML is the biggest a11y win: headers, buttons, labels
Keyboard-first test: unplug the mouse; if it fails, users are locked out

modules.title: JavaScript basics
modules.blurb: Types, functions, decisions, loops — the grammar of every interactive page.

lessons.title: Data types
lessons.objective: The basics of JavaScript data types.
keys: Primitives: string, number, boolean, null, undefined, symbol, bigint
const by default, let when reassigned — var is legacy
typeof tells you what you have; === compares what you mean

lessons.title: Functions and methods
lessons.objective: Managing an application's logic flow.
keys: A function is a named, reusable decision — inputs in, value out
Arrow functions: (a, b) => a + b — shorter scope, same idea
Methods are functions that belong to something (array.map, string.trim)

lessons.title: Making decisions with JS
lessons.objective: Conditions and logic branching.
keys: if / else if / else — the traffic lights of logic
Ternary for tiny choices: cond ? a : b; switch for many matches
Truthy/falsy: 0, '', null, undefined, NaN are false — memorize the five

lessons.title: Arrays and loops
lessons.objective: Working with collections of data.
keys: Arrays are ordered lists; index starts at 0
for, for...of, while — and map/filter as the loop with a purpose
push/pop at the end, shift/unshift at the head — know your costs

modules.title: Project — the terrarium
modules.blurb: HTML in practice, CSS in practice, and a drag-and-drop interface with the DOM.

lessons.title: Introduction to HTML
lessons.objective: Build the layout of an online terrarium.
keys: HTML is structure, not styling — elements describe meaning
div and span are the anonymous boxes; prefer named elements first
The terrarium: a positioned playground for the next two lessons

lessons.title: Introduction to CSS
lessons.objective: Style the terrarium, including responsiveness.
keys: The cascade: specificity decides which rule wins — id > class > element
Flexbox for one-axis layouts, grid for two
Position (relative/absolute) is how plants float over the terrarium glass

lessons.title: JavaScript closures and DOM manipulation
lessons.objective: Drag-and-drop with closures and the DOM.
keys: The DOM: the page as a tree JavaScript can rewrite
A closure is a function that remembers where it was born
pointer events + closures = drag-and-drop in vanilla JS

modules.title: Project — the typing game
modules.blurb: Event-driven programming: the keyboard becomes the controller.

lessons.title: Event-driven programming — build a typing game
lessons.objective: Use keyboard events to drive app logic.
keys: Events are the browser telling your code something happened
addEventListener wires reaction to event — don't poll, listen
Game state lives in variables; the DOM just displays the state

modules.title: Project — the browser extension
modules.blurb: How browsers work, forms, APIs, local storage, background tasks.

lessons.title: About browsers
lessons.objective: How browsers work, and scaffolding an extension.
keys: The browser: engine + renderer + JS runtime + storage, bundled
An extension is a webpage with permissions — manifest.json is its passport
Extensions prove the web platform is programmable end to end

lessons.title: APIs, forms and local storage
lessons.objective: Call an API from a form and persist variables.
keys: fetch: ask a server, await the answer, handle the failure
Forms collect; validation (client + server) protects
localStorage persists strings per-origin — settings survive reloads

lessons.title: Background tasks and performance
lessons.objective: Background processes and web performance.
keys: Service workers run behind the page — even when it's closed
Performance budget: every KB is someone's data plan
Measure first (dev tools), optimize second, assume never

modules.title: Project — the space game
modules.blurb: Advanced game development: classes, canvas, motion, collision, score, endings.

lessons.title: Advanced game development — inheritance and pub/sub
lessons.objective: Classes, composition and the pub/sub pattern.
keys: Classes template objects; inheritance shares behavior, composition delegates it
Pub/sub decouples: emitters don't know listeners exist
Game loop: update state → render → repeat, ~60 times a second

lessons.title: Drawing to canvas
lessons.objective: The Canvas API.
keys: Canvas is a pixel canvas: draw, clear, redraw — every frame
Screen coordinates: x grows right, y grows down
Images are sprites: load once, blit many

lessons.title: Moving elements around the screen
lessons.objective: Motion with cartesian coordinates.
keys: Motion = position + velocity × delta time
Deltas not absolutes: frame rates differ, physics shouldn't care
Edges collide first: clamp positions to the canvas bounds

lessons.title: Collision detection
lessons.objective: Make elements collide and react.
keys: Axis-aligned boxes: overlap on both axes = collision
Cooldown timers stop one hit from registering ten times
Collide → respond: damage, destroy, or bounce — decide in one place

lessons.title: Keeping score
lessons.objective: Math on game state, and performance.
keys: Score is state with an audience — update logic, then the DOM
Live score = constant mutation; constant mutation = constant care
Performance: touch the DOM in batches, not per particle

lessons.title: Ending and restarting the game
lessons.objective: End conditions and clean restarts.
keys: The end condition is a state like any other — won, lost, or paused
Restart = reset every variable, clear every timer, redraw the world
Games teach state machines; state machines run the world

modules.title: Project — the banking app
modules.blurb: A multipage app: routes, forms and validation, data flow, state management.

lessons.title: HTML templates and routes in a web app
lessons.objective: Scaffold a multipage app with routing.
keys: SPA routing: one HTML file, many views, hash or history API
Templates: write layout once, fill per page
Route = state; every route should be linkable

lessons.title: Build a login and registration form
lessons.objective: Forms and validation routines.
keys: Never trust client validation alone — the server re-checks everything
Password rules belong server-side; the client just previews them
Validation UX: precise messages, at the field, as you type

lessons.title: Methods of fetching and using data
lessons.objective: Data in, data out: fetch, store, dispose.
keys: fetch + await + try/catch — the holy trinity of data fetching
Every request fails eventually: design the failure UI first
Dispose what you fetch — memory leaks are silent until they aren't

lessons.title: Concepts of state management
lessons.objective: Retain and manage app state.
keys: State is the single truth; the UI is its projection
One-way data flow: events change state, state renders view
Global ≠ evil; untracked global IS — centralize and name it

modules.title: Extras — the editor and the AI assistant
modules.blurb: Using VS Code like a professional, and building your own AI chat project.

lessons.title: Use VS Code like a pro
lessons.objective: A code editor as a power tool.
keys: Command palette (Ctrl/Cmd-P) is the editor's keyboard
Extensions multiply the editor; settings sync keeps them yours
Integrated terminal + git panel = the workflow, undivided

lessons.title: Build your own AI assistant
lessons.objective: A first AI chat project in the browser.
keys: A chat UI is: history, input, and streaming answers
The system prompt sets the assistant's character and rules
Everything you built — state, fetch, events — is what AI apps are made of
